items.quote: Specimens were placed directly in sample holders made of alumina when the examining temperature was below 600 °C.

For terminal temperatures of 600 °C or above, specimens were encapsulated in evacuated quartz tubes and then placed in the sample holders to prevent oxidation and Zn evaporation. This technique was utilized by Vassilev [14] in his study of the Ni-Sn-Bi system. The apparatus was recalibrated by measuring the melting points of pure elements using the same setup. A base line was then determined by performing measurements on two empty quartz tubes. The temperature uncertainty was about ±1.0 °C.
The key phase compositions, however, were determined using the more accurate wavelength dispersive X-ray spectrometer (WDX).
Some critical alloys were carefully studied by analyzing XRD patterns generated using a D/max 2500 PC X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation and a step increase of 0.02° in the 2θ angle.
